teile.name: Hook
teile.text: How did Paramount's partner end up owning it? Ellison founded Skydance in 2010.
teile.szene: Painted open-world-game poster style: a blue-eyed man in a fedora, grey suit, dark tie and gold pocket watch stands in a dim modern film producer's office, a big studio lot glowing behind him, medium shot, warm light.

teile.name: Beleg
teile.text: For years, it co-financed Paramount films: Mission: Impossible, Star Trek and Terminator.
teile.szene: Painted urban game-poster style: a busy action film set at dusk, camera crane, crew and spotlights, a stunt performer silhouetted mid-leap over rooftops, wide cinematic shot, dramatic contrast lighting.

teile.name: Frage
teile.text: In 2023, Paramount's controlling shareholder explored deals. Skydance was one suitor.
teile.szene: Painted game-poster style: worried executives around a long boardroom table at night, city skyline in the window, one older executive staring down in thought, medium shot, cool blue light.

teile.name: Wendung
teile.text: Could it close? Talks collapsed in June 2024, then resumed that July.
teile.szene: Painted game-poster style: two executives turn away from a conference table in frustration, one chair pushed back, the fedora-wearing presenter watching from the doorway, close medium shot, tense cool light.

teile.name: Erklaerung
teile.text: July 7, 2024: a deal, with over $8 billion from Ellisons and RedBird.
teile.szene: Painted game-poster style: two executives in suits shake hands across a polished conference table as private investors watch, medium shot, warm amber light.

teile.name: Aufloesung
teile.text: It closed August 7, 2025. The financier Ellison became chairman and CEO.
teile.szene: Painted game-poster style: the fedora-wearing presenter with gold pocket watch looks up at a giant classic film studio water tower over a Hollywood lot at golden hour, low angle, warm light.

teile.name: Abschluss
teile.text: Be sure to like, share and save this video.
teile.szene: Painted game-poster style: the fedora-wearing presenter in grey suit smiles in a quiet projection room, film reels glowing behind him, medium shot, warm restrained light.

belege.name: Skydance
belege.text:
Skydance Corporation is an American multinational entertainment and media conglomerate that was founded on August 7, 2025. The company was formed through the merger of Paramount Global and Skydance Media and operated under the name of Paramount Skydance Corporation. Shortly after, it submitted several bids to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery, and the companies entered into an acquisition agreement on February 27, 2026, with the deal closing on October 6, 2026, after an extensive antitrust review and settlement. Upon the merger's completion, the company renamed itself as Skydance, and it operates Warner Bros. Entertainment and Paramount Pictures as separate film studios, along with an editorial board overseeing CBS News and CNN. 
David Ellison leads Skydance as its chairman and CEO, and the company trades on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol SKYD. Its primary corporate headquarters are located at One Astor Plaza in New York City, along with The Studios at Paramount in Los Angeles on the creative side. The company operates businesses across film, television, streaming, and interactive media, with its core streaming services being HBO Max and Paramount+
Larry and David Ellison own the majority of the company, with a 77.5% majority stake of Skydance's voting shares and 47.2% of all shares. Background: 

National Amusements: 
National Amusements was founded by Michael Redstone, and later passed to his son Sumner Redstone. After his death on August 11, 2020, the company was passed to a trust led by his daughter Shari Redstone.
It was a movie theater operator and mass media holding company incorporated in Maryland and based in Norwood, Massachusetts, controlled by the Redstone family. The company owned 69 theaters and 667 screens throughout the United States, the United Kingdom, and Latin America under several brands, such as Showcase Cinemas, Multiplex Cinemas, and Cinema de Lux. It was the controlling shareholder of Paramount Global.


Paramount Global: 
The origins of Paramount Global can be traced to Paramount Pictures, established in 1912, and the development of CBS and Viacom as major broadcasting and media businesses. Paramount Pictures was acquired by Gulf and Western Industries in 1966, while National Amusements, controlled by the Redstone family, acquired Viacom in 1987. Viacom subsequently acquired Paramount Communications in 1994 and merged with CBS Corporation in 2000.
In 2005, Viacom was divided into two publicly traded companies, CBS Corporation and Viacom. The companies reunited in December 2019 to form ViacomCBS, which was renamed Paramount Global in February 2022. The company operated film, television, streaming and broadcasting businesses, including Paramount Pictures, CBS, Nickelodeon, MTV, Paramount+ and Pluto TV.


Skydance Media: 
Skydance Media was founded by film producer David Ellison in 2010 as an independent film production and financing company. It developed a longstanding relationship with Paramount Pictures, co-financing and producing films in franchises including Mission: Impossible, Star Trek and Terminator. The companies renewed their production and distribution agreement in 2017.
Skydance expanded beyond feature films into television, animation and interactive entertainment. Its television division launched in 2013, while its interactive entertainment business was established following the acquisition of game developer The Workshop Entertainment in 2016. In 2017, the company expanded into animation through a partnership with Spain's Ilion Animation Studios. In February 2020, Skydance received a $275 million investment from RedBird Capital Partners and CJ ENM, valuing the company at $2.3 billion.


Warner Bros. Discovery: 
Warner Bros. Discovery was formed on April 8, 2022, through the combination of WarnerMedia, then owned by AT&T, and Discovery, Inc. The transaction brought together WarnerMedia's film, television, news and entertainment operations with Discovery's factual programming and international television businesses. Discovery, Inc. was renamed Warner Bros. Discovery, Inc., and the combined company began trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol WBD on April 11, 2022.
The company's businesses included Warner Bros. Pictures, Warner Bros. Television, New Line Cinema, DC, HBO, CNN, Cartoon Network, Discovery Channel, TLC, Food Network and Warner Bros. Games. Its streaming services included HBO Max and Discovery+. David Zaslav, previously chief executive of Discovery, Inc., became president and chief executive officer of the combined company.


History: 

Formation of Paramount Skydance (2023–2025): 
In 2023, National Amusements, the controlling shareholder of Paramount Global, began exploring potential transactions involving the media conglomerate amid financial difficulties and increasing competition in the entertainment industry. Several companies expressed interest in acquiring or partnering with Paramount, including Skydance Media, Sony Pictures, Apollo Global Management and Warner Bros. Discovery.
Negotiations between Paramount and Skydance initially collapsed in June 2024, but resumed the following month. On July 7, 2024, the companies announced a definitive agreement for a transaction involving the acquisition of National Amusements and the combination of Paramount Global and Skydance Media. The agreement included an investment of more than $8 billion from the Ellison family and RedBird Capital Partners. David Ellison, founder and chief executive of Skydance Media, was designated to lead the combined company, with Jeff Shell as president.
The transaction underwent regulatory review throughout 2025. The Federal Communications Commission approved the merger on July 24, 2025, clearing a major remaining regulatory hurdle. The combination was completed on August 7, 2025, establishing Paramount Skydance Corporation, with Paramount Global and Skydance Media becoming its subsidiaries. Ellison assumed the positions of chairman and chief executive officer, and the company's Class B shares began trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol PSKY.


Paramount Skydance (2025–2026): 
Following the merger, Paramount Skydance reorganized its operations into three principal business segments: studios, direct-to-consumer and television media. Its initial leadership included Andy Gordon as chief operating officer, Cindy Holland as chair of direct-to-consumer, George Cheeks as chair of television media, and Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein as co-chairs of Paramount Pictures. The company also revived Paramount Television Studios, combining the operations of Skydance Television and Showtime/MTV Entertainment Studios.
